short_title: ApoB vs LDL particle number when discordant (UK Biobank)

citation.title: Apolipoprotein B outperforms low density lipoprotein particle number as a marker of cardiovascular risk in the UK Biobank

access.full_text_source: Publisher HTML full text, academic.oup.com (doi:10.1093/eurjpc/zwaf554), opened in a browser; scripted access is blocked by the publisher

study.design_detail: UK Biobank participants with lipoprotein and apolipoprotein measurements. Concordance defined by a linear regression of ApoB on LDL-P with the intercept forced to zero; discordant subgroups were 2-30% above or below that line, compared with the concordant group.
study.population: UK Biobank adults with at least 10 years of follow-up data, three or more ICD codes and baseline characteristics

findings_summary: Among 41,099 UK Biobank participants, subgroups whose ApoB lay above the level predicted from LDL particle number had higher hazard ratios for MACE and CAD than the concordant group, increasing with the degree of discordance (HR 1.1 at 2%, up to 1.4 for MACE and 2.5 for CAD at 30%). Subgroups with LDL particle number discordant relative to ApoB showed no significant increase in hazard ratio (abstract wording: 'There was no significant increase in HR for CAD events or MACE for the subpopulations with discordant LDL-P vs ApoB').

limitations.text: LDL-P was measured with Nightingale Health's NMR platform (Methods: "a random subset of 121 540 blood samples was selected for metabolic profiling using Nightingale Health’s nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy platform (Helsinki, Finland)"). The authors: "One key limitation of our study is generalizability outside of the specific LDL-P assay used. The UK Biobank measured LDL-P with Nightingale Health’s NMR platform, which is one of several available technologies." Results may not transfer to ion-mobility LDL-P.
The authors state there is no standardization across LDL-P assays (Nightingale NMR, US NMR, ion mobility, VAP) and that these methods may yield discordant results.
Unable to adjust for medication use, especially statins; residual confounding cannot be excluded (authors).
The ApoB assay is not described in the paper; it is not verified here which UK Biobank ApoB measurement was used.

'Hazard ratios' are unadjusted case-rate ratios with Fisher's exact tests; no time-to-event model, covariate adjustment or confidence intervals are reported in the text. The comparator is described inconsistently: the Methods compare each subpopulation's case rate with the population case rate, while the statistical analysis paragraph refers to the concordant control group (see discrepancies).

The concordance coefficient is reported in the Figure 1 caption (LDL-P = 0.001168 x ApoB, intercept zero) without units. Its applicability to measurements from other assays, platforms or unit systems, including an ion-mobility LDL-P and an ApoB of unidentified method, has not been established.
Discordance is defined relative to a cohort regression line with the intercept forced to zero, not relative to laboratory reference ranges.
Selection on 10 years of data and three or more ICD codes, and a 95.1% white sample, limit generalisability.
Observational; relative hazard ratios only; no absolute risks in the abstract.
A published comment exists (Guillerme et al., Eur J Prev Cardiol 2026, doi:10.1093/eurjpc/zwag025); it has no abstract and was not reviewed.
'No significant increase' for LDL-P-discordant subgroups is absence of evidence of an association, not evidence that the discordance carries no risk; no confidence intervals are reported in the text.

applicability_constraints: UK Biobank participants (mean age 57, 95.1% white) with long follow-up records.
LDL-P was measured by Nightingale Health NMR, not ion mobility; the authors state the assays are not standardized and may disagree, so the findings do not transfer directly to an ion-mobility LDL-P.

Discordance percentages are relative to this cohort's zero-intercept line (coefficient 0.001168 in the study's own, unstated units, Nightingale NMR LDL-P); applying it to other assays or unit systems has not been established.
Group rate ratios are not an individual's risk.

discrepancies.description: Table 1 prints LDL-P as "0.0012 ± 3e-04" with the unit nmol/L, which is implausible for LDL particle concentration; the magnitude fits mmol/L (about 1200 nmol/L). The table's unit label is likely wrong.
discrepancies.handling: No claim uses the Table 1 LDL-P value; recorded only.

discrepancies.description: The comparator for the reported 'hazard ratios' is described two ways: "The hazard ratio (HR) of cases to controls was determined for the discordant subpopulations and the concordant control group" and "hazard ratios (HRs) were computed by comparing the subpopulation case rate with the population case rate". Which reference group produced the reported values is not resolved by the text.
discrepancies.handling: Claims state the reference group as inconsistently described; values are not presented as adjusted hazard ratios against a defined concordant group.

interpretation: In this cohort, ApoB carried the risk signal when the two measures disagreed in the direction of more ApoB than LDL-P predicted; the reverse direction was not significantly associated with events. LDL-P was measured by Nightingale Health NMR, which the authors state is not standardized against other LDL-P assays such as ion mobility, so transfer to an ion-mobility result is uncertain.
